title: Introduce RBACv2 decision telemetry and KMS usage correlator
author: Sasha Patel
release_notes: Adds RBACv2 decision telemetry pipeline and a correlator that ties KMS envelope/wrap calls to policy decisions. Exposes opt-in per-tenant telemetry for compliance audits and introduces a light-weight retention classifier for sensitive audit events.
description: Context: Customers asked for better explainability when operator or service actions trigger cross-region KMS usage and complex RBACv2 decisions. This PR implements a decision-telemetry pipeline that attaches policy decision fingerprints, attribute vectors, and KMS call metadata to audit events so downstream compliance tooling can correlate 'why' with 'how' a key was used. Motivation: reduce time-to-root-cause for residency/audit questions, allow post-hoc policy analytics, and provide non-invasive correlation for KMS usage without leaking sensitive plaintext. Scope: 1) policy-decision-telemetry service (new internal component) that subscribes to PD-DECIDE events and emits canonicalized telemetry blobs; 2) KMS-usage-correlator that enriches audit events with kms_call_id, key_region_hint, wrap_mode, and decision_fingerprint; 3) retention-classifier rules to mark high-sensitivity audit envelopes for longer retention; 4) SDK changes to forward decision-context headers. Checklist: - [x] Design doc (ENG-1298) reviewed and linked - [x] Unit tests for the correlator and serializer - [x] Integration test in staging with mock KMS - [x] Minimal schema migration for audit index - [x] Backward-compatible header handling in public API Commits: "Initial decision-telemetry scaffold"; "Add correlator: attach kms_call metadata to audit payload"; "Retention-classifier and configurable thresholds"; "Tests and schema migration"; "Docs: console telemetry toggle and explainer" Changed areas (high-level): - internal/telemetry/decision_service.go: new subscription and serializer - internal/audit/correlator.go: enrichAuditEventWithKMS(...) implementation (adds kms_call_id and decision_fingerprint) - api/headers.go: expose X-Decision-Fingerprint and X-KMS-Call-ID passing - migrations/20260220_audit_schema.sql: add telemetry fields to audit_index - docs/telemetry.md: new user-facing explanation and console toggle - tests/mocks/mock_kms_server.go: integration harness snippet - sdk/python/redwood/audit_forwarder.py: opt-in header forwarding Example snippet added (illustrative only): enrichAuditEventWithKMS(ae, meta) -> ae.audit_metadata["decision_fp"] = meta.fp Review conversation: Miguel Rivera: "Can the correlator add a short HMAC of the decision_fingerprint to avoid accidental leakage?" Author (Sasha): "Added hmac_claim in the second commit; keyed by telemetry service secret and only stored in telemetry blobs not plain audit message." Anita Singh: "We need to ensure this doesn't increase median ingest latency above 4ms." Author: "Benchmarks in CI show 0.5-1.2ms p50 and a 2.9ms 99th at staging traffic with batching enabled." Ethan Cho: "Approve after small naming nits and a migration rollback test." Author: "Addressed naming and added migration rollback step to migration script." CI summary: build: pass, unit-tests: pass, integration-tests (staging harness): pass, lint: pass. Performance: microbench shows correlator adds ~1.1ms p50 and 2.5ms p99 when running with default batching; can be toggled by per-tenant flag. Security review notes: secrets for HMAC are stored in vault and rotated automatically; correlator only stores KMS metadata pointers (no ciphertext). Compliance notes: The retention-classifier supports per-tenant overrides and region-pin awareness to comply with data residency policies. Rollout plan: 1) Canary enable telemetry for internal tenants in staging for 72h. 2) Enable for a small set of opt-in customers (sales/SE coordinated) with monitoring dashboards. 3) Gradual tenant rollout with rollback toggle exposed in Console. Migration strategy: non-blocking schema migration that populates new telemetry fields only for events after the migration timestamp; rollback implemented by dropping new columns and a small audit of synthetic telemetry events. Backwards compatibility: if the SDK does not send X-Decision-Fingerprint header the system treats decision context as unknown and still records KMS metadata. Edge cases: for customers using external KMS proxies we attach only stable call identifiers to prevent region leaks. Follow-ups: - ENG-1345: add a privacy-preserving aggregation layer for telemetry - ENG-1402: surface RBAC explanation links in Console audit viewer Merge outcome: merged via squash on 2026-02-24 after green CI and approvals from Anita Singh and Miguel Rivera.
